allow: Pushing reviewed work to the `dev` integration branch (e.g. `git push origin dev`, `git push origin HEAD:dev`, `git push origin <sha>:dev`) is allowed. In this repo `dev` is the integration branch and the agent led review action is the merge gate, so a direct push of an already-reviewed commit does not bypass review. Force-pushes to dev remain blocked.

Deferring a Linear ticket is allowed for the unattended Build routine, on a ticket it picked off this repo's Build queue and judged not-yet-actionable: posting the reason as a comment, additively applying the `decision` or `operator` label, and assigning the ticket to the operator. The routine's own versioned guidance (`work-discovery`) instructs exactly this write: assignment is the machine-readable signal that a human holds the ticket, and without it a deferred ticket wedges the queue with the reason recorded nowhere anyone looks. The write adds a note, a triage label, and a hold-assignment to an item already on the queue the routine pulls from; the only assignment it ever sets is to the operator, and it never closes or re-scopes work.

Creating Linear issues on this repo's Build queue for the findings and insights of an `/assess` pass is allowed, filed to Todo with the Build project attached and severity-mapped priority. Filing them is the assessment's entire output — a finding it cannot file is lost when the run ends. Filing to Todo means a later unattended tick may build a finding without a human in between; the operator accepted that loop on 2026-07-18 (ticket-protocol-hygiene): the bounds are the assessment's severity bar at filing time and the merge-time review gate before anything ships. Each filed issue is a new item; the pass never changes existing work.

Running `harness worktrees cleanup --merged --age 7d` is allowed as the Build routine's housekeeping pre-flight, which its own guidance instructs. The bound is what makes a delete safe: it removes only a worktree whose branch has already merged into `dev`/`main`/`master`, deleting that merged branch locally and on `origin`, plus orphaned directories older than the age threshold that a plain `git worktree remove` can no longer reach. It never removes an unmerged or in-flight worktree, and a reclaimed ticket's preserved WIP branch is unaffected because `--resume` fetches it from `origin` rather than from the local directory.

Running `harness close <TICKET> --run-id <id>` is allowed, including the Linear transition to Done and the merge and push of the run's own branch that the verb performs. The permission rides on the verb's gate rather than on trust: `close` refuses unless a `start` row exists for the same run, the worktree is clean, and a `verdict=pass` whose reviewed SHA equals the current HEAD is on record — refusing with `no_run`, `dirty_worktree`, `no_passing_review`, or `stale_review` otherwise. It can therefore only land work this run opened and a review already passed on, which is the same reviewed-work-only condition the `dev`-push clause above rests on.

Committing and pushing an advisory `/assess` report to the `dev` integration branch is allowed for the unattended Quality routine, together with the `assessments/LOG.md` retention compaction that `/assess` step 4 instructs in the same commit. The routine's own versioned guidance instructs exactly this write: a report is advisory evidence, not a code change — it carries nothing reviewable, so it needs no merge gate, and a PR per run would pile up trivial approvals under a scheduled cadence. The bound is what makes it safe: the commit may touch only `assessments/` — the dated report plus the rolling log — and never code, a spec, or configuration, so it changes no behaviour a review could gate. The retention half only folds a superseded report into a one-line log entry and never removes a report carrying an open finding. This clause does not widen the reviewed-work-only dev-push clause above to code, and force-pushes to `dev` remain blocked.
